user.title: Alert condition
user.description: Watch an exact state or numeric threshold, or add compound rules. Compound rules replace single-source matching and use ALL (AND) or ANY (OR). Numeric compound comparisons use raw source units and have no hysteresis. Profiles contain only shared delivery destinations and outputs.

data.name: Alert name
data.kind: Create an alert or a reusable profile
data.setup_action: Start with a new alert, copy, or YAML import

data_description.state: Underlying state string, such as on or open. Ignored when a numeric problem threshold is set.
data_description.numeric_below: Optional. Start when the value is strictly below this number. Leave both problem thresholds empty to match the state instead.
data_description.numeric_above: Optional. Start when the value is strictly above this number. Choose only one problem threshold.
data_description.numeric_recover_above: Optional. Keep the incident active until strictly above this value. Must be at least the problem-below threshold.
data_description.numeric_recover_below: Optional. Keep the incident active until strictly below this value. Must be at most the problem-above threshold.
data_description.numeric_unit: Exact unit attribute, for example %, °C, or °F. A missing or different unit suspends evaluation. Empty accepts the source's current units.
data_description.entity_id: Primary source for existing templates. Optional with compound rules; defaults to their first entity. Profiles do not watch a source.
data_description.conditions: Up to 20 rules. Empty uses the single watched entity. Unknown inputs follow the unavailable-source policy when known rules cannot determine the result.
data_description.setup_action: To duplicate or import, select it and continue; leave the other fields empty.
data_description.source: Watch an entity, or let Modern Alerts keep a schedule for a recurring task such as a filter change. A task ignores the entity and threshold fields on this form.

timing.title: Reminder timing and controls
timing.description: Add intervals in order. The last interval repeats indefinitely. Acknowledgement silences this incident; it does not disable the alert or reset its schedule.

data.evaluate_on_start: Evaluate the existing condition on startup
data.restore_state: Restore incidents after restart or reload
data.configure_delivery: Configure escalation, delivery rules, and history

data_description.intervals: One row gives a fixed interval. For example, 15, 30, 60 uses those delays in sequence, then repeats every 60 minutes. Minimum 0.016 minutes.
data_description.skip_first: When enabled, wait the first interval before notifying. Otherwise notify immediately when the problem begins.
data_description.evaluate_on_start: Start a new incident if the source already matches when the integration loads. Off preserves built-in Alert startup behavior. Restoring a saved incident takes precedence.
data_description.restore_state: Save acknowledgement, snooze, incident identity and deadlines. After source readiness, send at most one overdue reminder and resume the schedule. Off starts fresh after reload.
data_description.activation_delay: Require the problem to remain true for this long before creating an incident. Zero starts immediately. The first repeat interval begins after this delay.
data_description.recovery_delay: Require the recovery condition to remain true for this long before resolving. Reminders continue during this delay.
data_description.unavailable_policy: Resolve treats a nonmatching unknown/unavailable state as clear. Suspend preserves the incident and pauses reminders until usable data returns. Invalid numeric values always suspend. Single-entity numeric alerts always pause on an unknown, unavailable, or non-numeric value, whichever option is chosen, so a flaky sensor cannot report a false recovery.
data_description.enable_snooze: Allow the Snooze button and action. Snooze is separate from acknowledgement. A reminder is sent when the snooze ends, and the repeat interval restarts from then.
data_description.snooze_minutes: Used by the device and phone buttons, and by the snooze action when no duration is supplied. Maximum one week.
data_description.action_buttons: Add incident-specific Acknowledge, Snooze, and Open alert (and Done for recurring tasks) controls to direct mobile_app notify actions. Test and resolution messages have no generated controls. Automatic controls replace any actions in extra data for these destinations.
data_description.resolution_after_ack: Off suppresses resolution messages and recovery outputs when the incident is acknowledged. Cleanup still runs. Snooze does not suppress resolution.
data_description.configure_delivery: Open advanced delivery settings after Content. Leaving this off preserves existing settings.

notifications.title: Notification destinations
notifications.description: Select any number of destinations, or leave both lists empty for status only. Set up notification providers first. A missing destination is reported at dispatch and retried at the next reminder.

data.configure_outputs: Add or edit light, siren, speaker, and custom outputs

data_description.notifiers: Choose an action such as mobile_app_my_phone or persistent_notification. You can also enter a missing action name. Use a notify group for provider-specific top-level targets.
data_description.notify_entities: Uses notify.send_message. Home Assistant 2026.9.2 supports message and title only for these targets. Use a legacy action if you need extra data, tags, or action buttons.
data_description.configure_outputs: Open the output editor next. Leaving this off preserves existing outputs. Phone destinations may be empty when using device outputs.
data_description.profile_ids: Add shared destinations and outputs. Profile edits apply to every referencing alert at subsequent delivery opportunities. Unavailable profiles are reported on the status sensor.

messages.title: Notification content
messages.description: Enter plain text or Home Assistant templates. Leave message blank to use the alert name. A resolution notification requires an earlier alert attempt, including when the incident was subsequently acknowledged.

data_description.message: Rendered again for each notification. The alert name itself is literal text.
data_description.title: Optional, rendered for alert and resolution notifications.
data_description.done_message: Optional. For compatible Companion actions, use clear_notification with a stable tag in extra data to clear the notification.
data_description.data: Optional YAML mapping passed unchanged under the notifier data key. For example: tag: garage-door. Templates inside this mapping are not evaluated. Notify entities do not accept this field.

review.title: Review alert

outputs.title: Alert outputs
outputs.description:
Configured outputs: {outputs}

Combine outputs with phone notifications or use them on their own. Save the alert before testing an individual output from its device page.

output_remove.title: Remove output
output_remove.description: This removal takes effect when you finish and save the alert.

output_settings.title: Configure output
output_settings.description: Output type: {type}. Acknowledge and Snooze cancel running effects. Set the desired duration and cleanup behavior here.

data.name: Output name
data.restore: Restore previous light state or speaker volume

data_description.repeat: Off runs once per incident at its first notification opportunity. On follows the reminder schedule. An already-running effect is not duplicated.
data_description.duration: 0.1–300 seconds. Light and siren effects stop at this deadline. Speaker playback is stopped at this limit and may be cut short. Custom actions are time-limited and then run cleanup.
data_description.entities: Choose up to 20 entities. An unavailable or busy device is reported independently; other outputs still run.
data_description.pattern: Blink alternates on and off. Steady holds the selected light state for the duration.
data_description.interval: Used for Blink. Minimum 0.5 seconds; this is separate from the alert reminder interval.
data_description.restore: Restore lights or speaker volume on completion or cancellation, unless an external change was observed. Playback of previous media cannot be restored generically. With this off, lights are turned off and the chosen speaker volume is retained.
data_description.volume: Optional. Leave empty to retain the current volume. Supported settings depend on the device.
data_description.tone: Optional. Enter a tone supported by the selected sirens.
data_description.message: Optional. Defaults to the alert message. Templates can use alert_name, entity_id, incident_id, and message.
data_description.recovery_message: Optional. Spoken only when an incident with an earlier notification attempt resolves. Not sent on acknowledgement or snooze.
data_description.language: Optional language code supported by the selected TTS provider.
data_description.media_url: An audio URL reachable by the speaker, or a Home Assistant media-source URI.
data_description.media_type: Defaults to music. Override if your player requires another content type.
data_description.actions: Use the native action editor; no separate automation is needed. Variables: alert_name, entity_id (watched source), incident_id, and message.
data_description.stop_actions: Explicit cleanup for anything the custom actions leave enabled. Runs on duration expiry, acknowledgement, snooze, suspension, resolution, edits, or unload. Cleanup has a 10-second budget. These actions also run after an individual test.
data_description.recovery_actions: Optional separate sequence for resolution after an earlier notification attempt. Use self-contained actions; recovery sequences do not run the stop sequence afterward.
data_description.quiet_start: Optional daily quiet period in Home Assistant’s configured timezone. Both times are required. Overnight periods and daylight-saving changes follow the local clock.
data_description.quiet_end: Held alert delivery resumes within one minute after quiet hours, if the incident is still active and not acknowledged or snoozed. Recovery messages are skipped during quiet hours.
data_description.presence_entities: Optional. Person/device tracker home or binary/input boolean on means present. Leave empty to ignore presence. Unknown/missing states never prove everyone is away.
data_description.presence_mode: Any present: allow when at least one selected entity is home/on. Everyone away: allow only when all selected entities are known and neither home nor on.
data_description.weekly_windows: Deliver only inside these local-time windows. Empty allows all week. Overnight windows continue into the next day. Quiet hours and presence rules still apply. Start is inclusive; end is exclusive.

delivery.title: Escalation and delivery rules
delivery.description: Quiet hours and presence below apply to phone/notify destinations. Device outputs have their own rules. Escalation keeps the original destinations and adds each reached stage. Outputs assigned to a stage wait until that stage. Unassigned outputs are available from the start.

data_description.quiet_start: Optional daily quiet period in Home Assistant’s configured timezone. Both times are required. Overnight periods and daylight-saving changes follow the local clock.
data_description.quiet_end: Held alert delivery resumes within one minute after quiet hours, if the incident is still active and not acknowledged or snoozed. Recovery messages are skipped during quiet hours.
data_description.presence_entities: Optional. Person/device tracker home or binary/input boolean on means present. Leave empty to ignore presence. Unknown/missing states never prove everyone is away.
data_description.presence_mode: Any present: allow when at least one selected entity is home/on. Everyone away: allow only when all selected entities are known and neither home nor on.
data_description.group: Alerts with the same group, destination list, title, and provider data share a summary. Blank keeps alerts separate. Multi-alert summaries omit generated phone controls; use the alert device to acknowledge each incident. Single-alert deliveries retain phone controls. Grouping applies to alert notifications only.
data_description.group_window: Collect alert notifications for 1–300 seconds when a group is set. A new reminder replaces that alert’s pending message without postponing the existing group deadline.
data_description.rate_limit: Zero disables throttling. Otherwise coalesce reminders until this minimum interval has elapsed. Limits are shared by matching group/destination settings, and reset on Home Assistant restart.
data_description.history_limit: 0 disables history; otherwise keep up to 100 metadata entries. Default 50. History contains lifecycle/output events and error categories, not messages. Enable incident restoration to keep history across reloads.
data_description.stages: Add up to 10 stages with distinct elapsed-minute thresholds. Later recipients and outputs accumulate. Optional interval replaces the reminder cadence from that stage. Acknowledge stops escalation; snooze silences delivery without resetting incident age. After downtime, at most one catch-up delivery uses the latest reached stage.
data_description.weekly_windows: Deliver only inside these local-time windows. Empty allows all week. Overnight windows continue into the next day. Quiet hours and presence rules still apply. Start is inclusive; end is exclusive.

profile_review.title: Review reusable profile

duplicate.title: Duplicate an alert or profile
duplicate.description: Copy configuration into a new draft. Incident state, acknowledgement, history, and device identity are not copied. Review every step before saving.

import_yaml.title: Import legacy Alert YAML
import_yaml.description: Paste a single definition, named definitions, or an alert: section. Select one alert to review and create. No notification is sent by this preview. Disable the corresponding legacy alert before saving its replacement to avoid duplicate reminders. File includes and secrets must be expanded in the pasted text.

import_select.title: Choose an alert to import
import_select.description: One alert is created per workflow. Existing YAML and alert entities are not modified. You can edit all settings before the final review.

task.title: Recurring task
task.description: Choose when the task becomes due and how it can be marked done. Reminders, acknowledgement, snooze, and outputs are set on the following forms and work as they do for other alerts. Acknowledging only stops the reminders; the task stays due until it is completed.

data_description.task_mode: After completion counts the interval from when the task was last done. Fixed schedule follows a calendar rule. Once is a single reminder.
data_description.task_interval: After completion only. Intervals of a day or longer fall due at the time of day below; shorter intervals are exact.
data_description.task_time: The hour a task becomes due. For a fixed schedule this is when each occurrence starts, unless First due is set. Defaults to 12:00.
data_description.task_rrule: Fixed schedule only. An iCalendar rule such as FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=TU or FREQ=MONTHLY;BYMONTHDAY=1. Daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly rules are supported.
data_description.task_window: Fixed schedule only. The task is due from each start until it is completed or this much time has passed; an unanswered window is recorded as missed and reminders stop. Empty keeps the task due until completed.
data_description.task_first_due: Required for Once. Otherwise optional: seeds the first due date, and anchors rules such as every second week. Empty starts one interval from now, or at the next occurrence.
data_description.task_lead_days: Mark the task as upcoming this many days before it is due. This only sets an attribute; no notification is sent early.
data_description.task_tags: Scanning any of these tags completes the task. Copy the tag ID from Settings > Tags.
data_description.task_legacy_actions: Plain mobile action IDs that also complete the task, so existing notifications and shortcuts keep working during a migration.

error.invalid_repeat: Add at least one finite interval of at least 0.016 minutes that fits a valid notification date.
error.invalid_template: Enter valid Home Assistant template syntax.
error.invalid_destination: Use a specific notify action name or a notify entity. notify.notify and notify.send_message are not legacy destination names.
error.invalid_data: Extra data must be a YAML mapping, not a list or text.
error.entity_data_unsupported: Notify entities do not accept extra data in Home Assistant 2026.9.2. Clear this field, or choose only legacy notify actions.
error.invalid_duration: Enter a finite nonnegative delay that fits a valid date. Snooze must be greater than zero and at most 10080 minutes.
error.invalid_policy: Check both quiet-hour times, presence settings, stage thresholds, destination names, and finite values within the displayed limits. Stage thresholds must be distinct and greater than zero.
error.incompatible_thresholds: Choose one problem threshold and its corresponding recovery threshold. Recovery must be at or beyond the problem threshold in the recovery direction.
error.invalid_output: Check the output settings: choose valid entities, a name, finite values within the displayed limits, and any required provider or audio fields.
error.invalid_actions: Enter a valid Home Assistant action sequence. Check device actions, templates, and required fields.
error.invalid_conditions: Check the rule entities, comparisons, and values.
error.invalid_import: Invalid legacy Alert YAML. Paste only alert definitions, expand secrets/includes, and remove aliases or unsupported fields.
error.invalid_task: Check the task settings: choose a schedule type, a valid time and date, a lead time of 0 to 365 days, and at most 20 tags and action IDs. Profiles cannot be recurring tasks.
error.task_interval_required: Enter an interval of at least one minute and at most ten years.
error.task_due_required: Enter the date and time this one-off task is due.
error.invalid_rrule: Enter one iCalendar RRULE with a daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly frequency, for example FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=TU.

abort.invalid_name: The task could not be imported: check its name.
abort.invalid_task_mode: The task could not be imported: check its mode.
abort.invalid_task_interval: The task could not be imported: check its interval.
abort.invalid_task_rrule: The task could not be imported: check its recurrence rule.
abort.invalid_task_first_due: The task could not be imported: check its next due date.
abort.invalid_task_window: The task could not be imported: check its window.
abort.invalid_task_time: The task could not be imported: check its time.
abort.invalid_task_tags: The task could not be imported: check its tags.
abort.invalid_task_legacy_actions: The task could not be imported: check its legacy action IDs.
abort.invalid_notifiers: The task could not be imported: check its notify actions.
abort.invalid_notify_entities: The task could not be imported: check its notify entities.
abort.invalid_repeat: The task could not be imported: check its repeat intervals.
abort.invalid_message: The task could not be imported: check its message template.
abort.invalid_title: The task could not be imported: check its title template.
abort.invalid_done_message: The task could not be imported: check its resolution template.
abort.invalid_task_lead_days: The task could not be imported: check its lead time.
abort.invalid_source: The task could not be imported: check its settings.

error.invalid_policy: Check both quiet-hour times, presence settings, stage thresholds, destination names, and finite values within the displayed limits. Stage thresholds must be distinct and greater than zero.
error.incompatible_thresholds: Choose one problem threshold and its corresponding recovery threshold. Recovery must be at or beyond the problem threshold in the recovery direction.
error.invalid_output: Check the output settings: choose valid entities, a name, finite values within the displayed limits, and any required provider or audio fields.
error.invalid_actions: Enter a valid Home Assistant action sequence. Check device actions, templates, and required fields.
error.invalid_conditions: Check the rule entities, comparisons, and values.
error.invalid_import: Invalid legacy Alert YAML. Paste only alert definitions, expand secrets/includes, and remove aliases or unsupported fields.
error.invalid_task: Check the task settings: choose a schedule type, a valid time and date, a lead time of 0 to 365 days, and at most 20 tags and action IDs. Profiles cannot be recurring tasks.
error.task_interval_required: Enter an interval of at least one minute and at most ten years.
error.task_due_required: Enter the date and time this one-off task is due.
error.invalid_rrule: Enter one iCalendar RRULE with a daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly frequency, for example FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=TU.

acknowledge.name: Acknowledge
acknowledge.description: Silence reminders for the current incident until it resolves. Targets Modern Alerts status sensors.

unacknowledge.name: Resume reminders
unacknowledge.description: Clear acknowledgement and snooze. Resume on the existing reminder schedule without sending immediately.

turn_off.name: Acknowledge (turn off)
turn_off.description: Alias for acknowledge. Does not disable condition monitoring.

turn_on.name: Resume (turn on)
turn_on.description: Alias for unacknowledge. Does not force the problem to become active.

toggle.name: Toggle acknowledgement
toggle.description: Toggle acknowledgement of the selected alert.

test_notification.name: Test notification
test_notification.description: Send the current alert message explicitly, without changing incident or resolution eligibility.

snooze.name: Snooze
snooze.description: Silence reminders temporarily without clearing acknowledgement. A reminder is sent when the snooze ends. Omit minutes to use the alert default.

minutes.name: Minutes
minutes.description: Duration greater than zero and at most 10080 minutes.

cancel_snooze.name: Cancel snooze
cancel_snooze.description: End temporary silence without clearing acknowledgement or changing the reminder schedule.

test_output.name: Test selected output
test_output.description: Start one bounded output without creating an incident or sending phone notifications. Inspect output_errors for failures.

output_id.name: Output ID
output_id.description: Optional stable ID from the status sensor configured_outputs attribute. Omit to use the Output to test selector.

stop_outputs.name: Stop outputs
stop_outputs.description: Stop running effects and individual tests, including cleanup. Does not acknowledge the incident; repeated outputs may run at the next reminder.

clear_history.name: Clear incident history
clear_history.description: Delete this alert’s recent metadata history without changing the active incident or notification schedule.

complete.name: Complete task
complete.description: Mark a recurring task done. Resolves the current reminder and schedules the next due date. Acknowledging does not do this.

completed_at.name: Completed at
completed_at.description: Optional earlier time the task was actually done, for example yesterday. Interval tasks count from this time.

import_task.name: Import recurring task
import_task.description: Create a recurring task from existing values, so a current due date carries over exactly. Administrators only.

time.name: Time of day
time.description: When the task becomes due on its day. Defaults to 12:00.

window.name: Window
window.description: For fixed: how long each occurrence stays due.

next_due.name: Next due
next_due.description: The date and time the task is next due.

last_completed.name: Last completed
last_completed.description: When the task was last done.

lead_days.name: Lead days
lead_days.description: Days before due to mark the task as upcoming.

tags.name: Tag IDs
tags.description: NFC tags that complete the task.

legacy_actions.name: Legacy action IDs
legacy_actions.description: Plain mobile action IDs that complete the task.

notifiers.name: Notify actions
notifiers.description: Legacy notify action names, such as mobile_app_phone.

repeat.name: Repeat intervals
repeat.description: Minutes between reminders while the task is due.

done_message.name: Done message
done_message.description: Message sent when the task is completed.

action_buttons.name: Phone controls
action_buttons.description: Add Done, Acknowledge, and Snooze controls to Companion notifications.

options.any_home: At least one person or room is present
